events.title: Funeral of John F. Kennedy
events.description: Three days after his assassination in Dallas, President John F. Kennedy was buried at Arlington National Cemetery following a state funeral in Washington, D.C. that was watched by millions on television around the world.
events.significance: The funeral was a defining moment of national mourning in the United States and one of the first major events broadcast live to a global television audience, marking a turning point in American public life.

events.title: Evacuation Day in New York City
events.description: British troops left New York City, their last major military position in the United States, after the Treaty of Paris ended the American Revolutionary War. George Washington then entered the city with the Continental Army.
events.significance: The British withdrawal marked the practical end of British military occupation in the new United States and was celebrated in New York as Evacuation Day for many decades.

events.title: Einstein Presents the Field Equations of General Relativity
events.description: Albert Einstein presented the final form of his field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences in Berlin, completing his new theory of gravitation.
events.significance: General relativity transformed physics and cosmology, and it underpins modern understanding of gravity, black holes, and the expansion of the universe.

events.title: Independence of Suriname
events.description: Suriname gained independence from the Netherlands, becoming a sovereign republic on the northeastern coast of South America after centuries of Dutch colonial rule.
events.significance: Independence ended Dutch colonial presence in South America and established a new nation with a diverse population, though it was followed by political instability in the following decades.

events.title: Birth of Andrew Carnegie
events.description: Andrew Carnegie was born in Dunfermline, Scotland. He emigrated to the United States as a child and built a vast fortune in the steel industry before dedicating himself to philanthropy.
events.significance: Carnegie became one of the wealthiest people in history and funded thousands of public libraries, universities, and cultural institutions, shaping modern philanthropy.
